answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while signed votes expose equivocation. If k identities coordinate conflicting claims, correlated-equivocation penalties scale as O(k^2), so a sybil operator cannot dilute blame by splitting stake. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier increases capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation and forfeiture across linked escrows; even a gale of aliases, raven signatures, or umber accounts therefore raises rather than reduces attack cost.
